svg.text: WLD 205 DAY 6 — INSTRUCTOR KEY / DELIVERY GUIDE
Metallurgy Readiness I: Metal Properties + Material Behavior Vocabulary

g.text: 0–8 MIN — MATERIAL-PROPERTY SORT
Use the six Property Cards. Students match term → definition, then give the retrieval cue when provided.
Terms: hardness • strength • toughness • ductility • brittleness • thermal conductivity.
Correction cue: keep hardness separate from toughness; keep ductility separate from brittleness.
Move on when the student can identify the term without prompting.
8–20 MIN — PROPERTY MEANING IN WELDING / FABRICATION
Model one consequence or contrast for each property without starting the formal iron-carbon/transformation lesson.
Hardness: indentation/wear resistance, not toughness. Toughness: absorb energy before fracture.
Ductility: plastically deform before fracture. Brittleness: fracture with little plastic deformation.
Thermal conductivity: ability to conduct heat. Strength: use the broad source-pack definition only.
Instructor rule: explain the property word, not an unsupported grade-specific behavior or procedure value.
20–38 MIN — PROPERTY COMPARISON MATRIX
Students compare carbon steel, stainless steel, and aluminum using the authorized source and Day 6 matrix.
Require one supported baseline statement for each material family and one statement they cannot safely infer.
Samples/photos are observation aids only. Exact grade/alloy/temper must come from source documentation.
Use the Material Observation Sheet if samples/photos are staged.
Do not award credit for visual guessing that happens to land on the right answer.
38–52 MIN — MATERIAL-BEHAVIOR SCENARIOS
Scenario keys: bend before breaking → ductility; absorb impact energy → toughness;
rapidly carries heat away → high thermal conductivity; resists indentation → hardness.
For each scenario require: property word → supported conclusion → what cannot be concluded.
Coach only the failed reasoning step, then give a parallel prompt for immediate recheck.
52–60 MIN — METALLURGY VOCABULARY EXIT
Run the live exit independently with no coaching.
Review by domain: Property Vocabulary • Material Baseline / Source Control • Material-Behavior Scenarios.
Record only the unresolved domain. Do not repeat a domain already demonstrated successfully.
This bridge is prerequisite readiness, not formal Level II metallurgy completion or qualification evidence.
